security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate but high-risk local video rendering pipeline. Many static critical detections are false positives from visual theme names and documentation syntax, but the skill still performs real child-process execution, filesystem writes, symlink creation, CDN script loading, and runtime dependency downloads.

remediation.issue: Local command execution is required for transcription, matting, validation, and ffmpeg compositing.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running scripts, pin executable paths, and document every external binary invoked by the pipeline.

remediation.issue: Initialization and dependencies can update or download code and model artifacts from the network.
remediation.suggestion: Pin versions and hashes for packages, models, and global skill updates. Provide an offline or vendored mode for marketplace installs.

remediation.issue: Generated HTML loads GSAP from a public CDN in several templates.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor GSAP with integrity verification or load a reviewed local copy instead of executing remote CDN JavaScript.

remediation.issue: The pipeline creates project symlinks and writes generated outputs into user-selected directories.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict execution to a dedicated project sandbox and reject paths outside that sandbox before linking or writing files.

remediation.issue: Many bundled font binaries and one large CSS file were not statically scanned.
remediation.suggestion: Verify font provenance, retain license records, and scan binary assets with a dedicated artifact review process.

content.value_statement: Talking-head videos need captions that stay readable and match the scene. This skill builds timed caption layouts, matte-aware embeds, and final composites with local media tools.
actual_capabilities: Selects a caption identity from the included visual catalog.
Transcribes source video and creates word-level timing data.
Generates subject mattes so selected captions can appear behind the speaker.
Builds HTML caption animations for rail, cinematic, and themed styles.
Runs preview, timing, overflow, and occlusion checks before final rendering.
Composites rendered caption layers into a final video with ffmpeg.
limitations: Requires local hyperframes, Node, ffmpeg, and related media dependencies.
Best suited to one clear talking-head subject with stable framing.
May need network access for first-run model or package downloads.
Uses local shell scripts and should run only in trusted project directories.

use_cases.title: Caption Short Social Videos
use_cases.description: Add readable subtitles and a small number of embedded highlight words to creator clips.

use_cases.title: Style Founder Updates
use_cases.description: Turn a talking-head update into a polished captioned video with a consistent visual identity.

use_cases.title: Prototype Caption Treatments
use_cases.description: Preview multiple catalog identities before committing to a final rendered caption style.

prompt_templates.prompt: Build a cinematic caption plan with one strong embedded hero word per thought block. Keep ordinary speech readable on the rail.

output_examples.input: A 30-second founder update with one speaker and no existing subtitles.
output_examples.output: A captioned video with readable lower-third lines, one embedded highlight word, preview frames, and a final composite.

output_examples.input: A dark social clip asking for a neon caption style.
output_examples.output: A recommended neon-style identity, timed caption animation files, matte-aware placement, and an ffmpeg-rendered video.

output_examples.input: A bright tutorial clip where every word must be readable.
output_examples.output: A conservative rail-first caption treatment with contrast checks and minimal embedded emphasis.

best_practices: Run the decision gate before authoring any caption plan.
Use embedded hero words sparingly and keep most speech on readable rails.
Preview frames and fix timing, occlusion, and overflow before final render.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill on clips with multiple speakers or hard cuts without splitting them first.
Do not embed every spoken word behind the subject.
Do not run the scripts on an untrusted project folder or unreviewed media.

faq.question: Does this skill edit the original footage?
faq.answer: It composites caption layers over the source video. The main footage is not meant to be recolored or restyled.

faq.question: What video works best?
faq.answer: A single talking-head clip with clear speech, a visible face, and stable framing works best.

faq.question: Can it make every word cinematic?
faq.answer: It can, but the skill recommends readable rails for most words and embedded effects only for key moments.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: It may need network access for first-run dependency, model, or package downloads.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. It executes local media tools and should require user confirmation and a trusted workspace.
